newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade surplus widens in September. [CORRECTED 10:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German trade surplus widens in September. [CORRECTED 10:20 GMT]

text.p: Germany's trade surplus widened slightly to 8.3 billion marks in September and the current account deficit narrowed to 1.6 billion marks, the Federal Statistics Office said on Tuesday.
German exports totalled 64 billion marks in September, up from 58.4 billion marks in August, while imports also rose to 55.7 billion marks from 50.3 billion.
In August, the trade surplus was 8.1 billion marks and the current account deficit 4.6 billion.

The services account showed a deficit of six billion marks in September, up slightly from a deficit of 5.7 billion in August, while the deficit in wealth and property income rose to 2.9 billion marks from 800 million marks.
Over the first nine months of the year so far, Germany's trade surplus widened to 69.1 billion marks compared to 61.2 billion marks in the first nine months of 1995.
(Corrects both figures for nine month period).
The current account deficit during the period also widened to 23.0 billion marks from 21.0 billion in the first nine months of 1995.
